eval_mode_reason: correction 20 / D-F: attn_dropout=0.2 makes a train-mode alpha stochastically zeroed, and reward refuses the trace. The control runs in eval too or the arms differ in two things.
expectation: PRE-REGISTERED. (1) capture_off lands within noise of e0c's 310 +/- 2 sent/s for the RSR arm -- not as a denominator, but as the prediction the amendment names. Expect capture_off to be FASTER than 310 because the policy here is FIFO (e0c measured FIFO at 374 +/- 8), so the honest prediction is ~374, and if it is not, the harness has drifted from e0c's. (2) capture_on is SLOWER than capture_off by a visible margin -- the bridge does 6 einsums of [B,M,H,Dh]x[H,Dh,D] per step plus B python-level trace constructions. (3) capture_off is byte-identical in LOSS to a pre-change run: capture is observation. (4) r_i on top of the bridge costs LESS than the bridge itself, because it is 6x[H,M,D] norms against 6 projections.
falsifier: F-capture-free: 'capture is off by default and free when off.' Falsified if capture_off after this change is outside the spread of a capture_off run with the bridge code absent, or if observe() runs at all with observe=False. Secondary, and the brief's bar item 3: 'the capture actually contains W_O' is falsified if zeroing/dropping W_O leaves r_i unchanged -- run as a mutation, not as a timing.
policy: FIFOPolicy subclass with an observe counter
seed_meaning: torch.manual_seed(rep) before model construction; the DATA is seed 0 in every repeat, so the seeds vary initialisation, not the workload shape. A timing repeat is not a statistical seed and this run does not claim it is.
